2027 Applications Are Now Open!
We are pleased to share that there are no application fees for our PhD, MS, or Graduate Certificate programs. We encourage you to take advantage of this opportunity and submit an application.
For information about our programs, please click below:
Request more information
To be considered for our graduate programs, a student must have:
1. Earned an undergraduate degree from an accredited institution prior to the first semester of proposed graduate study, except for qualified undergraduate students applying from the accelerated “4+1” MS programs
2. A minimum cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) for most programs; some programs set higher GPA thresholds. Applicants below the 3.0 minimum may still be considered based on the strength of other application components.
3. The School of Science and Engineering does not require GRE scores for review by the department. Applicants who have taken the GRE may include their scores on the application.
General Guidelines and Admissions Requirements for Graduate Programs
Step 1
Complete the online application.
Apply Now
Step 2
Upload the required materials.
Personal Statement
Please read the prompt provided within the application before writing your personal statement.
References/Recommenders*
All applications require you to provide information for your references. Make sure that you have the correct contact information for each of your references. An incorrect email address for your references will delay your application from being reviewed by the admissions committee. Recommendation Letters should be sent directly from the reference using the special link that is provided for them within the Slate application. If a reference is having an issue connecting to Slate using their special link and/or uploading their recommendation letter, they can contact segrad@tulane.edu.
Step 3
Submit transcripts.
Student copies (unofficial copies) of your transcript are acceptable during the application process. Admitted students must submit official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions to register for classes. Official transcripts must be sent from the university/college or a third party vendor such as Parchment.
Step 4
Complete additional requirements.
Please carefully review your individual program of interest for any additional admissions requirements beyond those listed here.
* Please note that the application deadline is for you to submit your application on time. Recommenders can submit their recommendation letters after you submit your application and after the application deadline.
Students who receive financial support and/or special tuition discounts will have this information included in their award/admission letter.
You are required to notify the Tulane Financial Aid Office of your receipt of school/program awards, as they will need this information to determine your eligibility for any federal assistance (U.S. residents).
Tulane Science & Engineering Accelerated “4+1” Programs
Qualified Tulane Science & Engineering students and consortium students may have an opportunity to earn a master’s degree in one year following the completion of their bachelor’s degree. School of Science & Engineering allows up to six (6) credit hours of graduate credit to be counted toward both the undergraduate and graduate degree for students admitted to the Accelerated (4+1) MS programs. If a student takes additional graduate credit above the 120 hours required for the undergraduate degree, up to six (6) additional credit hours may be counted toward the graduate degree for a maximum of twelve (12) credits.
Students interested in 4+1 programs should meet with the Graduate Studies Director of the academic programs or contact Associate Dean Ilianna Kwaske at ikwaske@tulane.edu.
Incentive for 4+1 Students
1. Enrollment deposit is waived.
2. If a student completes 12 credits of graduate credit while they are an undergraduate student, they have 18 credits remaining for the MS degree, which can be completed in one year.
3. A student can complete the MS degree in one year for less than $38,000 (please note that this is based on 2026-2027 tuition and fees).
For Tulane 4+1 students, once you are officially enrolled as a 4+1 MS graduate student, you will no longer be eligible for your undergraduate financial aid scholarships. Tulane 4+1 students must graduate with their undergraduate degree from Tulane prior to formally being enrolled in the 4+1 Master's program.
All Undergraduate tuition scholarships and awards are not applicable toward the tuition for the MS or PhD programs within SSE.
Not Ready To Apply?
If you are not ready to apply - or the application for the program you wish to apply to is not available, - please click below, and someone will respond back to your request for more information.
Request More Information
MS Student Support
The MS Programs are tuition-based programs, and students are required to pay tuition and all required fees. The latest information regarding tuition rates and fees can be found on the Tulane Accounts Receivable page. Government employees enrolled in any Tulane Science & Engineering MS programs are eligible for a reduced tuition rate.
Higher education is an investment in your future. You may be eligible for financial aid to help cover the costs of tuition, books, fees, or other expenses associated with your education. Students seeking financial aid to help pay for the master’s program should visit the Office of Financial Aid page for School of Science & Engineering Students. US residents can apply for federal student loans and other support by completing the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA).
The School of Science and Engineering offers a few scholarships for MS Programs. Teaching or research assistantships to students in the MS programs are generally not offered.
Students awarded a scholarship or special financial support, will be notified in their offer of admission that will be posted in your status portal.
Any Special Tuition Rates and/or Special Scholarships that are included in your letter of admission for an MS program within the School of Science and Engineering are not transferable to another program. Any support offered is program-specific and not transferable (including assistance provided within the same department and similar program).
Ph.D. Student Support
The School of Science and Engineering offers Teaching Assistantships and/or Research Assistantships to all incoming PhD students. PhD students are typically admitted with a full tuition waiver, 50% support toward the purchase of a Tulane-sponsored Student Health Insurance Plan (T-SHIP) health insurance plan and a stipend that is associated with either a Teaching Assistantship or Research Assistantship. Incoming PhD students are expected to pay the academic service, student activity, and recreation center fees that are billed during the fall and spring semesters.
Scholarships 360
Tulane University partners with Scholarships 360 to provide current and prospective students with access to external scholarship opportunities to help cover their cost of attendance. Graduate students should be sure to search by grade level to find scholarships to help pay for the MS programs.
Learn More
Yellow Ribbon Program
Tulane School of Science & Engineering participates in the Post-9/11 GI Bill Yellow Ribbon Program and provides up to $5,000 per year for 20 graduate students. More information about the Yellow Ribbon Program is on the Office of the Registrar’s page.

FAQs
Do you charge application fees for graduate programs?
We do not charge application fees for PhD programs, MS programs or Graduate Certificate programs.
Can I apply to more than one program?
Yes, you can apply to more than one program. You will need to complete an application for each program.
Do I need to send you official copies of my transcript?
We do not require official transcripts to apply to a program. However, if you are accepted into the program, you must submit official transcripts to Tulane School of Science and Engineering before you register for your graduate coursework. The address and information required to submit official transcripts is included in the letters of admission.
Can I use my undergraduate transcript if my Bachelor's Degree has not been posted on it as I will be graduating in the near future?
Yes, you can send us your current transcript. Your official transcript with the degree posted must be sent from your institution prior to beginning your graduate program. If you have not graduated with your bachelor's degree, your admission will be revoked, as you cannot pursue your graduate degree unless you have already earned your undergraduate degree.
Can I submit my application if the recommenders have not uploaded their recommendation letters?
Yes, you should submit your application. The application deadline applies to the applicant and not the recommenders/references. Your references/recommenders will be able to respond and upload their recommendation letters to your application after the deadline.
Can I submit my recommendation letters from my recommenders?
No, recommendation letters should come from the recommenders themselves. If they have any issues or concerns with the emailed link, they can email their recommendation letter to segrad@tulane.edu, and it will be uploaded to your application. Make sure they include your full name in the email so that the correct application will be updated.
Do I need a potential advisor before I submit my application?
No. However, it is helpful to identify at least one faculty member who has a background and research in the area in which you are most interested in studying.
Do I need to take the GRE?
The GRE is not required.
Do I need to take the TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo English Test?
English Language Proficiency
All graduate applicants are required to demonstrate English proficiency for admission consideration. There are two ways to meet this English language proficiency requirement:
Prior education – A bachelor’s degree or higher from an accredited university located in the U.S or another country in which English is both the primary spoken language of daily life and the language of instruction or at least two years of full-time study at such an institution. If you meet either of these criteria, you are exempted from submitting English proficiency test scores. Please be sure to include such information and transcripts in your application.
Exam score – If you do not meet the criteria in 1, you must certify proficiency in English when you apply. Tulane University accepts the Internet-based Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL iBT), International English Language Testing System (IELTS), and the Duolingo Test for English Proficiency academic exams.
Minimum overall score on TOEFL iBT: 87.
Minimum overall band score on IELTS Academic: 7.0.
Minimum overall score on Duolingo Test for English Proficiency: 120. Note: Duolingo will not be accepted for PhD applicants, only MS applicants.
This requirement applies to U.S. citizens and Permanent Residents as well as international applicants.
If you are admitted, you may also be required to confirm your proficiency prior to arrival.
Should I review the department websites?
Yes, you should take time to review the information regarding the graduate programs and admissions requirements that can be found on the department websites. Departments may have additional information that they require during the application process.

When will I receive an updated status on my application?
You can check your status using the status portal that is created once you submit your application. Applications are typically reviewed after the application deadline. Most graduate admissions decisions are made on or before April 15th.
I am currently a Tulane undergraduate student, how does the 4+1 program work?
The School of Science & Engineering allows up to six (6) credit hours of graduate credit to be counted toward both the undergraduate and graduate degree for students admitted to the Accelerated (4+1) MS programs. If a student takes additional graduate credit above the 120 hours required for the undergraduate degree, up to six (6) additional credit hours may be counted toward the graduate degree for a maximum of twelve (12) credits.
